title.en: The Shop That Opened With a Crooked Sign

caption.en: The place next door was still picking a sign.
caption.ko: 옆 가게는 아직 간판을 고르는 중이었다.

en: The sign was still crooked when he opened.

moral.en: Starting was never about the size of the decision. It was about how long deciding took.
moral.ko: 시작은 결정의 크기가 아니었다. 정하는 데 걸린 시간이었다.

cta.en: One decision you keep putting off sets tomorrow's order.
cta.ko: 미룬 결정 하나가 내일의 순서를 바꾼다.

subtitle.en: Crooked sign, end of the alley

narration.en: It was a shop at the end of an alley. He opened with the sign still crooked. That was all.
narration.ko: 작년 겨울, 골목 끝 가게였다. 간판이 비뚤어진 채 문을 열었다. 그게 다였다.

image_hint.en: narrow alley at dusk, one person walking past a small storefront with a crooked sign, seen from behind, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: narrow alley at dusk, one person walking past a small storefront with a crooked sign, seen from behind, long shot

subtitle.en: The shop next door, still dark

narration.en: The shop next door had no lights. A paper was taped to the door. It said opening soon.
narration.ko: 옆 가게는 불이 꺼져 있었다. 문에 종이가 붙어 있었다. 곧 연다고 적혀 있었다.

image_hint.en: dark shop window at night, one person standing outside reading a paper note on the door, distant figure

scenes.image_prompt: dark shop window at night, one person standing outside reading a paper note on the door, distant figure

narration.en: I passed both shops every morning. Almost nobody went in. He moved the chairs around anyway.
narration.ko: 나는 두 가게를 번갈아 봤다. 손님은 거의 없었다. 주인은 매일 의자를 옮겼다.

image_hint.en: small restaurant interior in the morning, one person wiping tables and shifting chairs, seen from behind, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: small restaurant interior in the morning, one person wiping tables and shifting chairs, seen from behind, long shot

narration.en: Three months went by. The crooked sign hadn't moved. The note next door was fading.
narration.ko: 석 달이 지났다. 비뚤어진 간판은 그대로였다. 옆 가게 종이는 바래고 있었다.

image_hint.en: street corner in winter, one person walking past two shopfronts, distant figure, long shot

subtitle.en: He didn't buy a new one

narration.en: Then one morning the sign sat straight. He hadn't bought a new one. He just tightened the screws.
narration.ko: 어느 날 간판이 반듯해져 있었다. 새로 산 게 아니었다. 다시 조여 붙인 것이었다.

image_hint.en: shop front in daylight, one person on a ladder fixing a sign, seen from behind, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: shop front in daylight, one person on a ladder fixing a sign, seen from behind, long shot

narration.en: Someone said the broth was salty. By next week it wasn't. The menu board changed quietly too.
narration.ko: 국물이 짜다는 말이 나왔다. 다음 주에 간이 달라져 있었다. 메뉴판도 조용히 바뀌었다.

image_hint.en: small kitchen at night, one person stirring a pot, seen from behind, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: small kitchen at night, one person stirring a pot, seen from behind, long shot

narration.en: He decided first and thought after. There was no meeting. Wrong things got fixed on the spot.
narration.ko: 그는 정하고 나서 생각했다. 회의는 없었다. 틀린 건 그 자리에서 고쳤다.

image_hint.en: restaurant counter in the afternoon, one person writing on a chalkboard menu, distant figure, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: restaurant counter in the afternoon, one person writing on a chalkboard menu, distant figure, long shot

narration.en: That's when I looked at my own desk. My plan was still on page one. I wrote that line last winter.
narration.ko: 나는 그제야 내 책상을 봤다. 계획서는 첫 장에 멈춰 있었다. 작년 겨울에 쓴 문장이었다.

image_hint.en: desk by a window at night, one person sitting with an open notebook, back to the camera, long shot

scenes.image_prompt: desk by a window at night, one person sitting with an open notebook, back to the camera, long shot

narration.en: This morning I read the same line again. The pen was right there. I didn't touch it.
narration.ko: 오늘 아침에도 그 문장을 읽었다. 펜은 옆에 그대로 있었다. 손은 대지 않았다.
